rationale: Third item in 'gift of well-being / gift of wisdom / gift of ⲛⲟⲁⲙ.' The lexeme is irregular; possibly a Lycopolitan variant of ϫⲟⲙ ('power, might'). Confidence low. May warrant comparison with the German edition (Polotsky/Böhlig) for an established reading.
ⲧϩⲧⲟⲉ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩϣⲏ = 'the fourth (part) of the night,' a watch. Standard Coptic ϩⲧⲟⲉ 'fourth, quarter.'
Lycopolitan collective form of the numeral 'four' (= Sah. ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ). Used here for 'the Four Great Days.'
Standard Coptic ⲣⲙⲙⲁⲟ 'rich one.' The 'Twelve Great Rich Gods of the Greatness' is the technical Manichaean designation of the Twelve Aeons / Twelve Great Aeons of Light.
Verb of bearing/supporting, used twice (lines 24, 27) of the Pillar of Glory bearing the cosmic burdens (ⲍⲣⲏϣⲉ). Possibly related to a Coptic root for 'lift, raise.' Tentative.
Greek loanword κλίμα — the four cosmic 'climes' or quarters. Standard term in Manichaean cosmology.
Greek στῦλος + Coptic ⲉⲁⲩ. Technical Manichaean title for the Great Omophoros (Atlas figure) who bears the refined light upward through the cosmos.
